```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, comment = NA)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
```

This tutorial introduces to data augmentation with the package `housepi`.
We explain the process of associating augmented variable to individuals to then proceed with standard model generation and inference.

# Estimate Incubation Periods Distribution

For simplicity, we start testing data augmentation on a dataset which is not a household survey.
Instead we consider a simulated report documenting the days when a number of cases were exposed to infection and the days of symptom onset.

Assuming the incubation period to be described by a gamma distribution, we want to estimate the respective parameters augmenting the exposure and onset times, modeled as uniformly distributed in the reported ranges.
We associate a positive status to all individuals and we correct for right censoring modifying the maximum values as follows:

```{r}
dataset <- housepi::delays
dataset$exposure_max <- dataset$exposure_max + 0.999
dataset$onset_max <- dataset$onset_max + 0.999
dataset$status <- 1
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(head(dataset))
```

We generate the model as showed in the [Walkthrough](walkthrough.html):

```{r}
# generate an instance of the household model class
hmc <- housepi::HouseholdModelClass$new("eg-augm-incubation-from-delays")

# gamma distribution parameter definitions
hmc$load_param_list(
  shape = list(value = 2,
               prior = "unif", 
               args = list(min = 0, max = 5),
               rule = "norm", 
               rule_scale = 1),
  scale = list(value = 1.1,
               prior = "unif", 
               args = list(min = 0, max = 5),
               rule = "norm", 
               rule_scale = 1)
)
```

## Build Augmented Variables

Similarly to parameter definitions, for augmented variables we provide a DataFrame or a file with the models and proposer rules needed for the Bayesian Monte Carlo.
However, augmented variable definitions are more delicate, since they can depend on the dataset or on model parameters.
We state which value should be imported from the dataset by formatting the string with the value header: "*header_name*`@D`".
Here we associate to each individual an exposure and an onset time.

```{r}
# add 'exposure' time definition
hmc$add_augm(
  name = "exposure",
  value = "exposure_min@D", # start from data value 'exposure_min'
  min = "exposure_min@D",   # move within the range 'exposure_min'
  max = "exposure_max@D",   # and 'exposure_max'
  rule = "norm",            # normal distribution for the proposer rule
  rule_scale = 0.25         # with scale 0.25 (i. e. standard deviation)
)

# add 'onset' time definition
hmc$add_augm(
  name = "onset",
  value = "onset_max@D",
  min = "onset_min@D",
  max = "onset_max@D",
  rule = "norm", 
  rule_scale = 0.25
)
```

We run the inference and we extract the results

```{r}
hmc$infer(dataset = dataset, n_steps = 1e5, n_burnin = 1e4, 
          thin = 10, n_adapt = 2500, seed = 4349, id_trace = 5)
```

Note: The warning tells us that our dataset has no demographic structure: 
it will be interpreted as single individuals living in separate households.

```{r, fig.width=6, fig.height=4, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, out.height="auto", fig.align="center"}
lattice::xyplot(hmc$traces)
```

## Other Proposer Rule for the Augmented Variables

```{r}
# use default "blank" model to show some tests
hmc <- housepi::HouseholdModelClass$new("blank")
```

```{r, fig.width=6, fig.height=4, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, out.height="auto", fig.align="center"}
# with model (default Gibbs rule)
hmc$drop_all()
hmc$add_augm(name = "move_with_model", model = "norm")
lattice::xyplot(hmc$infer(progress = FALSE, seed = 31)$traces)

# random walk starting from 0 (without model)
hmc$drop_all()
hmc$add_augm(name = "random_walk", value = 0, rule = "norm")
lattice::xyplot(hmc$infer(progress = FALSE, seed = 31)$traces)

# independent normal moves from value 5 (without model)
hmc$drop_all()
hmc$add_augm(name = "independent_moves", rule_from = 5, rule = "norm")
lattice::xyplot(hmc$infer(progress = FALSE, seed = 31)$traces)
```
